        Chicago White Sox manager Will Venable and Brewers manager Pat Murphy were named the Managers of the Year in their respective leagues on Tuesday night as part of the BBWAA's awards week. Murphy is the first manager to ever win the award in three consecutive seasons.The annual awards, which also include Manager of the Year, Reliever of the Year, Cy Young and MVP, are voted on by 30 members of the Baseball Writers Association of America (that's two per MLB city in each league). Votes were submitted before the beginning of the playoffs, meaning that only regular-season contributions are taken into account.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    National League: Pat Murphy, BrewersMurphy, manager of the World Series champion Milwaukee Brewers, has been voted the National League Manager of the Year, the Baseball Writers Association of America announced on Tuesday. He is the first person to win three consecutive Manager of the Year awards and the tenth person with three Manager of the Year wins in total.Ballots for the BBWAA's awards are submitted between the end of the regular season and the beginning of the postseason. They are regular-season awards and Milwaukee's World Series win did not factor into the voting.
Of course, Murphy did not need the World Series win to boost his Manager of the Year case. He guided the small-market Brewers to baseball's best record (103-59) and run differential (+214) during the regular season, and their fourth consecutive NL Central title. Their 103 wins are a franchise record and baseball's most since 2023.Manager1st2nd3rdPointsPat Murphy, Brewers2073124Walt Weiss, Braves716386Don Mattingly, Phillies131125Craig Stammen, Padres211124Dave Roberts, Dodgers217Craig Counsell, Cubs13Don Kelly, Pirates11Murphy just completed his third season as Brewers manager and has three Manager of the Year wins to show for it. Bobby Cox (2004-05), Kevin Cash (2020-21), and Stephen Vogt (2024-25) are the only others with two consecutive Manager of the Year awards. Vogt was not an American League Manager of the Year finalist this season.Prior to Murphy's threepeat here, the Brewers had never had a Manager of the Year winner. He's won the award now three times in three years at the helm.
Atlanta Braves manager Walt Weiss and Philadelphia Phillies manager Don Mattingly finished behind Murphy in the voting. Mattingly took over as an interim after the Phillies fired Rob Thomson on April 28. Philadelphia had baseball's fourth-best record after the managerial change. Weiss guided the Braves to the NL East title.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    American League: Will Venable, White SoxVenable, who helped orchestrate a 24-win year-to-year improvement and guided the team to its first postseason berth since 2021, has been named the American League Manager of the Year, the Baseball Writers Association of America announced on Tuesday. He beat out Tampa Bay Rays manager Kevin Cash and Boston Red Sox manager Chad Tracy.The White Sox went 84-78 in 2026 after going 60-102 in 2025 and a hideous 41-121 in 2024. Those 121 losses are the record in baseball's Modern Era (since 1900). Venable's White Sox are the first team in history to reach the postseason after losing at least 100 games in the previous two seasons (they also lost 101 games in 2023).
The huge steps forward seem to be what secured the award for Venable. He took over in 2025 and the White Sox improved by 19 wins that season, only to turn around and improve by 24 more wins this past season. They were arguably the most surprising playoff team in 2026 and Venable gets his due here. Manager1st2nd3rdPointsWill Venable, White Sox15113111Kevin Cash, Rays1212298Chad Tracy, Red Sox351747Stephen Vogt, Guardians169Aaron Boone, Yankees114Joe Espada, Astros11Venable joins the following White Sox manager of the year winners: Ozzie Guillen, 2005Jerry Manuel, 2000Gene Lamont, 1993Jeff Torborg, 1990Tony La Russa, 1983Cash finishes as the runner-up in a very close vote. Tracy finishes in third place, with Guardians manager Stephen Vogt fourth and Yankees' skipper Aaron Boone sitting fifth. Cash's Rays improved by 21 games to win an AL-best 98 and win the AL East after finishing in fourth place in 2025. title: NFL trade deadline aftermath: Which teams improved, which teams should have made moves - CBS Sports
description: The 2026 NFL trade deadline came and went Tuesday afternoon at 4 p.m. ET, and the league provided a flurry of activity. Of the NFL's 32
body:
The 2026 NFL trade deadline came and went Tuesday afternoon at 4 p.m. ET, and the league provided a flurry of activity. Of the NFL's 32 teams, 23 teams combined to make 18 trades, with 19 players and 34 picks changing hands in 2026. That is right in line with the average of 19.3 traded midseason since 2019, which is way up from the average of 7.5 between 2009 and 2018. The volume of trades wasn't the only thing that has increased around the trade deadline lately. There have been 11 future first-round picks swapped since 2019, up exponentially from the three that changed hands from 2001 to 2018. Three first-round picks alone were traded in 2026, with All-Pro defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons going from the Tennessee Titans to the Chicago Bears (two) and defensive tackle Jordan Davis going from the Philadelphia Eagles to the Jacksonville Jaguars (one).So which teams improved and which teams should have made moves? Let's dive into a 2026 NFL trade deadline evaluation on who did well and who should have done more. 
Teams that improved
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Jacksonville JaguarsThe Jaguars smell blood in the AFC waters. On Monday, the Jaguars relinquished a 2027 first-round pick, a 2027 second-round pick, a 2028 fifth-round pick, a 2028 sixth-round pick and a 2029 second-round pick for the services of Philadelphia Eagles Super Bowl champion defensive tackle Jordan Davis, Atlanta Falcons Pro Bowl safety Jessie Bates III and New Orleans Saints defensive tackle Davon Godchaux.   It makes sense. The Jaguars are right to go all in for the 2026 season. The Buffalo Bills (7-1) have one of the leakiest secondaries in the NFL, allowing 238.8 passing yards per game (fourth-most in the NFL). The Denver Broncos (7-2) have offensive inconsistency issues because of quarterback Bo Nix. His 5.6 air yards per pass attempt is mere decimal points ahead of Kansas City Chiefs (6-2) quarterback Patrick Mahomes' 5.6 air yards per pass attempt to avoid being dead last in the league. However, Mahomes' figure has more to do with the Chiefs' limited passing-game options than with an unwillingness to throw the ball downfield, as with Nix.The AFC North-leading Pittsburgh Steelers (6-2) have Aaron Rodgers at quarterback, and he will be 43 years old by the time the playoffs begin. Jacksonville beat the Cincinnati Bengals (6-2) in a narrow, one-score game earlier this season, and the New England Patriots (5-4) just got decimated at home (45-27) by quarterback Jordan Love and his Green Bay Packers.
Jacksonville's timing is definitely right: They have the NFL's No. 4 scoring offense (28.6 points per game) and the NFL's No. 2 scoring defense (15.1 points per game). Quarterback Trevor Lawrence has what he needs to soar, and now his defense does too. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Minnesota VikingsThe Minnesota Vikings (6-2) needed to make a trade for a quarterback after the monstrosity that was their Carson Wentz-led offense in a 23-6 loss on "Monday Night Football." Wentz completed just 8 of his 25 throws for 81 yards and two interceptions for an 8.9 passer rating. That's right, Wentz's 8.9 passer rating is not a typo. It is the worst passer rating by a Vikings quarterback in a game since 1984, when Tommy Kramer registered a 7.5. Wentz's 32% completion percentage is tied for the worst in a game in Vikings history, which is how the Vikings recorded their lowest time of possession (17:28) in 40 years. 
It would have been a slap in the face to defensive coordinator Brian Flores and his No. 1 scoring defense (14.5 points per game allowed) for the Vikings not to trade for a quarterback. Minnesota did what they had to do Tuesday by sending a 2027 third-round pick to the Las Vegas Raiders to acquire old friend Kirk Cousins. At the age of 38, Cousins ranks second in the NFL in touchdown passes in 2026 (20), three behind Joe Burrow's and one ahead of Jordan Love. That's also eight more passing touchdowns than the total number of touchdowns the Vikings' offense has this season. Twelve offensive touchdowns is tied for the fewest by a team with a 6-2 record or better through eight games played since 1950. The good news is four-time Pro Bowl wide receiver Justin Jefferson's production should return with Cousins. In the only fully healthy season the duo shared in 2022, Jefferson won NFL Offensive Player of the Year honors after leading the league in targets (184), catches (128), receiving yards (1,809), and receiving first downs (83). The 98.9 passing yards per game that Cousins averages to Jefferson is the most by a quarterback-receiver duo in NFL history (min. 50 games). Minnesota definitely improved on Tuesday.
Most receiving yards per game by QB-WR duo, NFL history (minimum 50 games played)Receiving YPGMIN Kirk Cousins/Justin Jefferson98.9HOU Matt Schaub/Andre Johnson97.1DET Matthew Stafford/Calvin Johnson95.6
                            
    
                                                
                    
    San Francisco 49ers  The NFC-leading San Francisco 49ers (7-1) bolstered their two biggest areas of weakness — defensive tackle and wide receiver — with two highly decorated veterans: three-time Pro Bowl defensive tackle DeForest Buckner and six-time Pro Bowl wide receiver Keenan Allen. The great news is San Francisco didn't have to invest too much draft capital into either player, sending the Indianapolis Colts a 2027 fourth-round pick for Buckner and a 2027 sixth-round pick for Allen. Buckner's 4.0 sacks through nine weeks are tied for the seventh most in the NFL among defensive tackles, while his 22 quarterback pressures rank as the 15th most among defensive tackles. That's fantastic production for any player, let alone a 32-year-old the 49ers know incredibly well after he played the first five seasons of his career in San Francisco. Allen, whose 12,402 career receiving yards rank as the fourth most in the NFL among active players, is a nice, reliable depth addition for a 49ers receiver room that can't manage to stay healthy. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Buffalo Bills Buffalo led the NFL in scoring defense with 19.3 points per game allowed from 2021 to 2025 under ex-head coach Sean McDermott, but under first-year defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard, they're allowing 23.4 points per game, ranking 16th in the league. They're also 14th in expected points added (EPA) per play and 17th in EPA per dropback, but those numbers were artificially deflated by Wentz and the wheezing Vikings offense on Monday. Through the first eight weeks of the season, the Bills were tied for 24th in scoring defense (25.9 points per game allowed), 24th in defensive EPA per play and 27th in EPA per dropback. Enter Titans safety Amani Hooker, whom they acquired along with a 2027 fifth-round pick in exchange for a 2027 second-round pick.  Hooker, who is 28 years old, leads the NFL in interceptions (5) after picking off Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow three times in an overtime defeat in Week 8. The Bills could certainly see Burrow in January. Hooker is just the third player in the past 40 years with 50-plus tackles (52) and five-plus interceptions (5) in his first seven games of a season, along with Washington cornerback DeAngelo Hall (2010) and Colts linebacker Cato June (2005). He and Green Bay Packers All-Pro safety Xavier McKinney are also the only two players in the last three seasons with 200-plus tackles (204) and double-digit interceptions (10). Acquiring Hooker also came at a steep price. His three-year, $40.5 million contract is now a team-friendly asset that has him under team control through the 2028 season. On Monday night, Minnesota had open wide receivers throughout the game, but Wentz was unable to find them. That won't be the case against stiffer quarterback competition in the postseason. Teams are throwing at Buffalo's secondary at the second-highest rate in the NFL (62.6%) as they are allowing the fourth-most passing yards per game (238.8) in the league, per NFL Pro. That's why Buffalo parted with a second-round pick to acquire Hooker.  
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Philadelphia EaglesGeneral manager Howie Roseman built two Super Bowl championship teams with the Eagles in 2017 and 2024, and he may be well on his way to doing so again after his wheeling and dealing in 2026. The Eagles have 10 picks in the first two rounds across the next three drafts — five first-round picks and five second-round picks.Roseman turned wide receiver A.J. Brown, defensive tackle Jordan Davis and offensive lineman Cam Jurgens into two first-round picks, two second-round picks and two fifth-round picks. The Eagles have their own first-round pick and second-round pick, plus the Jaguars' first-round pick in 2027. They have their own first-round pick and own second-round pick plus the New England Patriots' first-round pick (A.J. Brown trade) and the Baltimore Ravens' second-round pick (Cam Jurgens trade) in 2028. In 2029, they have their own first-round pick, their own second-round pick and the Jaguars' second-round pick (Jordan Davis trade).    Even though the Eagles have lost seven in a row since their 2-0 start and Super Bowl MVP quarterback Jalen Hurts is out for the season with blood clots, Roseman has Philadelphia primed to bounce back toward Super Bowl contention sooner rather than later. 

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Tennessee Titans The Titans have won just one of their first eight games this season, indicating they are still far off from contending despite spending an NFL-most $333.9 million in free agency in the 2026 offseason. That's why they traded two of their best defensive players for significant hauls.First, they sent All-Pro defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons and a 2028 fifth-round pick to the Bears in exchange for a 2027 first-round pick, a 2027 fourth-round pick and a 2028 first-round pick. Then, they sent Hooker and a 2027 fifth-round pick to the Buffalo Bills for a 2027 second-round pick. Now, the Titans have four first-round picks — their own plus the Bears' 2027 and 2028 firsts — and three second-round picks — their own plus the Bills' 2027 second — in the next two drafts. That should hopefully get Tennessee out of rebuilding purgatory. 

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Kansas City ChiefsThe Chiefs (6-2) are always in win-now mode, with Mahomes (31 years old), tight end Travis Kelce (37), defensive tackle Chris Jones (32), defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo (66) and head coach Andy Reid (68) getting up there in age. Kelce, Rashee Rice, who is coming back from an offseason knee surgery, and former first-round pick Xavier Worthy haven't been getting the job done. Kansas City is averaging 117.5 receiving yards per game by wide receivers this season, which is the fewest of the Mahomes era (since 2018) and ranks 28th in the NFL this season. That's why the Chiefs went out and traded for Downs. The 25-year-old Downs has been a weapon out of the slot since entering the league as a third-round pick in 2023: His 1,995 yards receiving out of the slot are the second most in the entire NFL in the span of his career, trailing only Detroit Lions All-Pro wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown (2,160). Most receiving yards from the slot, since 2023Receiving yards from the slotAmon-Ra St. Brown2,160Josh Downs*1,995CeeDee Lamb1,970Trey McBride1,966Jaxon Smith-Njigba1,766* Downs was drafted in the third round of the 2023 NFL Draft
Yes, Downs is a rental playing out the final year of his rookie contract in 2026, but Kansas City had a dire need. Plus, if Downs builds a nice rapport with Mahomes, this deal could lead to a second contract come the 2027 offseason. It's also a huge win that the Chiefs didn't have to part with any Day 2 draft capital. This move should give Kansas City's passing game a much-needed jolt. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Indianapolis ColtsOnce the Colts fired general manager Chris Ballard after Week 6, the Indianapolis fire sale was on. They traded away four players in the past two weeks, the most by any team in a season in the past 25 years. They made the most trades (four) and acquired the most draft picks (six) of any team this season. As a result, the Colts now have 11 picks in the highly anticipated 2027 NFL Draft, although they still lack a first-round pick. That belongs to the New York Jets thanks to Indianapolis' 2025 NFL trade deadline mistake of sending their 2026 and 2027 first-round picks to the Jets in exchange for cornerback Sauce Gardner. The next general manager the Colts hire will have those 11 draft picks to rebuild the franchise. Indianapolis did decide to retain three-time Pro Bowl running back Jonathan Taylor, which may make sense given he is 27 years old — young enough to be a major contributor for a rebuilt Colts offense through the 2028 season. Taylor averages 88.8 rushing yards per game, the fifth-best average in NFL history.

    Los Angeles ChargersThe Los Angeles Chargers' position toward the 2026 NFL trade deadline made no sense. They're the NFL's last winless team at 0-8, and they had a number of veterans on expiring contracts they could have shopped. Nine-time Pro Bowl edge rusher Khalil Mack at 36 years old is certainly at the top of the list, but cornerback Donte Jackson and defensive tackle Dalvin Tomlinson also could have been moved. Perhaps even former first-round pick wide receiver Quentin Johnston could have been shipped over for draft capital. Los Angeles completely fumbled by only trading away linebacker Daiyan Henley to the Denver Broncos for a 2027 fourth-round pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick. They should have joined the Colts and Titans in tearing down much of their current roster. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Green Bay PackersGreen Bay is dead last in the NFL in rushing offense (68.2 rushing yards per game) while leading the league in dropped passes with 23, seven more than the next closest team — the Los Angeles Rams. Love has also been hit 57 times this season, the fifth most in the league. Despite all that adversity, he leads the NFL in passing yards (2,618) and completions of 20-plus yards (40) and is third in passing touchdowns (19). With the Packers winning five of their last six games to improve to 6-3 in 2026, Love deserves more support. Whether that's along his battered offensive line or at running back — another position beset by injuries — getting him more help in the ground game could have been a game changer for the Packers' postseason hopes. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Arizona Cardinals   The Arizona Cardinals are 3-6 in the NFC West, which means their 2026 season is already cooked in terms of playoff hopes. Arizona has already lit premium draft capital on fire at luxury positions. Remember: It drafted running back Jeremiyah Love third overall in the 2026 NFL Draft while having plenty of other glaring needs. Not trading eight-time Pro Bowl safety Budda Baker at the age of 30 while clearly rebuilding is an epic whiff. The same can also be said for 29-year-old Pro Bowl edge rusher Josh Sweat.

title: NFL trade deadline: Ranking all 18 in-season deals as Kirk Cousins, Jeffery Simmons reshape Super Bowl race - CBS Sports
description: The Jaguars, Bears and Bills are among the teams that pulled off home-run moves
body:
The Jaguars, Bears and Bills are among the teams that pulled off home-run moves
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 10, 2026
                            
                    at
    8:27 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            12 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The fourth-most active trade deadline in NFL history is complete. Teams completed 18 in-season moves by the time the clock struck 4 p.m. ET on Tuesday as they positioned themselves for postseason runs and rebuilds. The biggest blockbusters that defined the deadline sent star defensive tackles to Super Bowl contenders and quarterback help to sputtering offenses, and those should prove with time to be the most impactful deals of the year.Some moves that occurred well in advance of the deadline have already paid dividends. Jeffery Simmons, for instance, is already a difference-maker for the Chicago Bears and was integral in their building a four-game winning streak. Others delivered mixed results, as is the case with the Quenton Nelson and Joey Porter Jr. deals since both players are dealing with injuries early in their tenures with the Seattle Seahawks and Dallas Cowboys, respectively. As for those that flew in just ahead of the deadline, the next few weeks will determine which teams won or lost their trades.Trades are about more than just coming away with more talent than the other team involved. Evaluating the impact of a transaction comes down to specific team needs, the capital sent back in return and how the move addresses short-term contention prospects and long-term roster outlooks.With those factors in mind, below are all 18 in-season trades ranked from most to least impactful.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    1. Vikings acquire QB Kirk CousinsThere was one missing piece in Minnesota that, if found, could turn the Vikings into a force to be reckoned with in the Super Bowl race. It took until the last minute, but they found it. Kirk Cousins promises to give the Vikings the offensive lift they need to capitalize on their league-best defense. This year has been a renaissance for the 38-year-old who is on pace to threaten for his first 40-touchdown season. That late-career surge and his familiarity with the offense in Minnesota should allow him to step right into action and help the Vikings avoid the tight, low-scoring battles of the campaign's first nine weeks and start blowing opponents out. His arrival ought to also unlock Justin Jefferson and turn him back into the superstar-level producer he is meant to be.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    2. Bears acquire DT Jeffery SimmonsThere is a strong case to be made that Jeffery Simmons is the best in-season acquisition, because he already proved to be a game-changer for the Bears. The impacts of the other trade deadline moves are speculative, while Simmons' is known. He wreaked all kinds of havoc over his first two games in the middle of the Chicago defensive line, was paramount in the Bears' win over the Seahawks and was one of the few reasons why they survived their five-turnover disaster on "Sunday Night Football" in Week 9. The three-time All-Pro turned the defense into a significant asset overnight. That is a transformational impact that will help this team maximize its potential with Caleb Williams leading the charge on the other side of the ball.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    3. Jaguars acquire DT Jordan DavisThe Jaguars were one of just two teams to trade a first-round pick. They also packaged a 2029 second-rounder to land Jordan Davis. It was a high price, but that was to be expected, since Davis is a franchise-building block who signed a contract extension with the Eagles earlier this year and will be under team control for three years beyond this one. The trade should pay dividends both straight away and over the long term as the Jaguars step into their championship-contention window. It was about as big of a swing as Jacksonville could have made in the wake of the torn quad that knocked DaVon Hamilton out for the year. They did not just replace Hamilton; they upgraded.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    4. Jaguars acquire S Jessie Bates IIIThe impact Jessie Bates III delivers to the Jaguars' defense in 2026 might be even greater than that of Davis, but he checks in one spot lower in the rankings because of the potential short-term nature of his stay in Jacksonville. The star safety is in the final year of his contract and may turn out to be a rental. If that is all he is, then the secondary will enjoy every minute of his half season in town, because as a three-time All-Pro, there are few defensive backfield stalwarts as talented as he is. Bates elevates the starting lineup but also minimizes the impact of losing Eric Murray for the season due to an elbow issue. Pass defense has been one of the few knocks against the otherwise elite Jaguars, as they rank 22nd in slowing teams down through the air. This helps immensely in that regard.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    5. Bills acquire S Amani HookerAmani Hooker is tied for the league lead in interceptions and already has five takeaways for the second time in three years. That kind of turnover prowess in the defensive backfield through 2028 is worth spending a second-round pick and a fifth-round pick. The Titans captain has allowed a passer rating of just 79.3 this season, which is his best mark since his rookie season in 2019. For a Bills team that scores at will and just needs its defense to hold up its end of the bargain, Hooker's arrival raises the floor and the ceiling. Safety was a need after the Bills released C.J. Gardner-Johnson, and they filled it in an emphatic way.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    6. 49ers acquire DT DeForest BucknerThe 49ers' reunion with DeForest Buckner addressed a serious deficiency on the defensive line, where injuries once again reared their ugly heads. Alfred Collins and CJ West remain on injured reserve, and Gracen Halton just suffered a season-ending ankle fracture in Buckner's first game back in the Bay Area. San Francisco can seemingly never have enough playmakers amid its never-ending injury woes. Bringing Buckner back was more than just insurance, though. It is a step up in the trenches, which will aid the NFC West leaders as they pursue a championship.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    7. Giants acquire QB J.J. McCarthyJaxson Dart's season is over, but the Giants' campaign is far from done. Even though the J.J. McCarthy trade did not make all the sense in the world when it happened, it has aged phenomenally, with the third-year quarterback stepping up as a commendable replacement for the injured starter. McCarthy is 2-0 as a starter and is playing the best football of his career (albeit in a small sample size) and has done nothing but keep the Giants comfortably in first place in the NFC East. This is not a long-term answer for New York since Dart will reclaim the No. 1 job next year, but if it allows the Giants to win the division and flip McCarthy -- or keep him as a renowned backup -- then it is a massive victory in the face of unfortunate circumstances.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    8. Ravens acquire QB Jacoby BrissettThe jury is out on whether Jacoby Brissett can keep the Ravens afloat until Lamar Jackson returns from thumb surgery. On one hand, he has been a premier backup for years and should be far more capable of directing the ball in the way of Zay Flowers and Derrick Henry than Joe Fagnano was in his spot start. But on the other hand, the Cardinals benched him before they moved on from him. This was a desperation trade for the Ravens that, if it pays off, will result in them remaining on the fringes of postseason contention. If Brissett is nothing more than a bottom-tier starter, though, Baltimore can kiss this season goodbye.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    9. Seahawks acquire G Quenton NelsonQuenton Nelson underwent a minor knee procedure to remove loose bodies in his knee, which is a hiccup in his young Seahawks tenure and slightly downgrades the value of the trade. The expectation should be for Nelson to return within a couple of weeks and play at an All-Pro level. But he did not impress in his debut in Seattle, will miss at least some time, and is set to become a free agent at the end of the year, so the amount of time he spends making a real impact in the trenches could be slim when it is all said and done. The Seahawks need his supreme blocking ability in the lineup to help jump-start their dormant run game.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    10. Cowboys acquire CB Joey Porter Jr.When he is on the field, Joey Porter Jr. is a lockdown corner for the Cowboys. But he missed his first game upon arrival in Dallas with an illness and missed time over the last two weeks with an ankle issue, and it is not as if the middling defense was all that much better overall in the four games he did play to date. Unless Jerry Jones re-signs Porter in the offseason -- and that seems like a stretch given Porter's demands and Jones' typical unwillingness to pay a premium to keep free agents -- this will be a rental situation. A rental with trouble staying on the field. It looks clear that the Cowboys were more than just a standout cornerback away from figuring things out on defense.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    11. Chiefs acquire WR Josh DownsKansas City would have had no excuse for coming away from the trade deadline without a wide receiver. Chiefs wideouts account for just 46.0% of the team's receiving yards, which is the second-lowest rate in the NFL. Josh Downs could help take some of the pressure off the tight end group and running back Kenneth Walker III in the receiving department and perhaps free up Rashee Rice and Xavier Worthy to become greater big-play threats. In order for the Chiefs to truly be back to their Super Bowl-contending ways, they have to be more balanced on offense. Downs' arrival, at the very least, will not hurt in their quest for more passing production.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    12. Ravens acquire C Cam JurgensThe Ravens were in a tough spot at center when Tyler Linderbaum left in free agency and found their answer in early October when they made a play for Cam Jurgens, a two-time Pro Bowler and a Super Bowl champion who was part of the Eagles' legendary run at offensive line. Early returns on the trade are underwhelming, though. Jurgens is already up to 16 pressures allowed this year and was hit with multiple penalties in the early going, which is no recipe for success in an offense that has churned through quarterbacks behind him. Some of the troubles can be chalked up to the underwhelming guard play next to him, though.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    13. 49ers acquire WR Keenan AllenA rash of injuries devastated San Francisco's wide receiver group over the first half of the season and emphasized the need for even more bodies in what went from a deep group to a thin one in short order. When Mike Evans and Deebo Samuel Sr. are healthy, Keenan Allen projects as an ideal third option for MVP-contending quarterback Brock Purdy. He was the top-producing receiver in Indianapolis on a per-game basis, so he clearly still has something to give in the latter stages of his career. Expect Allen to command a sizable role in the immediate future before potentially giving way to De'Zhaun Stribling when he returns from injured reserve and serving as a depth piece and ready-made starter when his number is called.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    14. Texans acquire WR Marvin Harrison Jr.When the Texans took a shot on Marvin Harrison Jr., it made all the sense in the world. Their wide receiver group needed a No. 2 receiver to step up; the Cardinals were clearly out on him as part of their future, and he has tons of experience working with C.J. Stroud dating back to their time together at Ohio State. There is still time for him to turn his career around, especially since he remains under contract through 2028. But even with a touchdown in one of his first three games in Houston, Harrison has done little to command a consistent role. The Texans may have given up a second-round pick and a fifth-rounder for someone who will remain behind Nico Collins, Xavier Hutchinson, Kayshon Boutte, Jaylin Noel and Tank Dell in the pecking order.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    15. Broncos acquire LB Daiyan HenleyThe Broncos should feel great about taking a starting inside linebacker away from a division rival, even if it came at the cost of two draft picks. Daiyan Henley projects to step back from his starting job with the Chargers and assume a rotational role behind Alex Singleton and Justin Strnad, so he will be a premier second-string option at the position on an already stout defense. This is the kind of move that will fly under the radar so long as Henley plays off the bench, but one that makes a rich unit even richer and gives Denver meaningful depth on the road to a deep playoff run. 

                            
    
                                                
                    
    16. Lions acquire S Andre CiscoThe NFL's worst pass defense is a little less bleak now than it was before the Andre Cisco trade, but the move might not move the needle enough to make a meaningful difference in the Lions' inability to keep opponents off the field. Cisco can step into the lineup next to Brian Branch, but this has the look of more of a depth addition as Detroit awaits the return of Kerby Joseph. The latter's insertion back into action will do far more to improve upon the Lions' 260.9 passing yards allowed per game than Cisco. Joseph will either be activated by Nov. 17 or shut down for the rest of the year. In that sense, the Cisco move makes plenty of sense. But the Lions would, of course, prefer not to rely on him as a starter.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    17. Jaguars acquire DT Davon GodchauxHad the Jaguars stopped at the Davon Godchaux trade, they would have plugged a hole on their defensive line with a space-eating run stopper and pulled off a one-for-one replacement for the injured DaVon Hamilton. Of course, they proceeded to land Davis hours later, thus reducing the importance of the Godchaux deal. In the end, this comes out as a depth addition on a defensive line that is in flux but one that should be among the league's best at defending the run. Jacksonville is in a tremendous spot as it surges toward the No. 1 seed in the AFC.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    18. Ravens acquire OL Ryan NeuzilIt came as a surprise to see the Ravens make a last-minute move for another center, since they had already acquired one in Jurgens just over a month ago, but they landed Ryan Neuzil and pried him away from his starting job with the Falcons. Neuzil has ample experience at guard, so he could shift over to the left side of the line and replace John Simpson. He may also become the team's top reserve on the interior and one capable of playing at either guard spot or at center should he be thrust into action. Time will tell how the Ravens deploy him, and until then, the grade on the deal is incomplete.

title: 2026 NFL trade deadline grades for every team: Four teams earn an A, Rams and Chargers among disappointments - CBS Sports
description: The 2026 NFL trade deadline has come and gone, a whirlwind of activity changing the NFL landscape halfway through the season. After coun
body:
The 2026 NFL trade deadline has come and gone, a whirlwind of activity changing the NFL landscape halfway through the season. After countless rumors, reports and hypothetical moves, there were 18 trades between the beginning of the regular season and the trade deadline, including six on deadline day itself.A quarterback reunion stole the show on Tuesday, with Kirk Cousins heading back to the Vikings in exchange for a third-round pick going to the Raiders. It's the second quarterback deal by Minnesota this year; the Vikings also sent J.J. McCarthy to the Giants. And if the postseason started today, McCarthy's Giants would host Cousins' Vikings in a wild-card matchup.Defensive tackle, normally not a headlining position, was in the spotlight, with the Bears acquiring Jeffery Simmons from the Titans and the Jaguars acquiring Jordan Davis from the Eagles. Also on the move at the position were DeForest Buckner and Davon Godchaux.Sometimes, though, it's the moves not made that tell a bigger story. Here's how all 32 teams fared with trade deadline grades for everyone in the league.
AFC East
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Buffalo Bills: B+The Bills saw several other Super Bowl contenders making significant win-now moves and decided to make their own on deadline day, acquiring safety Amani Hooker and a 2027 fifth-round pick from the Titans for a 2027 second-round pick. It's a big move for a player in the middle of his best year: Hooker has five interceptions this year, including three off Joe Burrow in one game. Other Bills safeties have one pick combined. He is a versatile defender who's willing to tackle -- a strong addition to a Bills secondary that needed help. It was expensive, but worth doing. Buffalo got significantly better Tuesday.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Miami Dolphins: C-It was a rough deadline day for the Dolphins: Quarterback Malik Willis landed on IR, and veteran defensive tackle Zach Sieler -- a potential trade candidate -- is done for the season with ruptured biceps. The timing couldn't have been worse regarding Sieler. It might have been nice for this one-win team to get some compensation there.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    New England Patriots: D+The Patriots not making any moves was a bit of a surprise considering Rhamondre Stevenson is hurt (knee), TreVeyon Henderson is dealing with an illness, and the offensive line and wide receiver group are truly beat up. This felt like a chance for New England to improve Drake Maye's surroundings, even if it was just via modest improvements, but New England didn't make any moves.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    New York Jets: B+The Jets got a sixth-round pick for trading Andre Cisco to the Lions but held otherwise. That was probably the right move, even with Will McDonald IV asking for a trade amid decreased playing time. If needed, they can act on that request this coming offseason. The Jets already did tremendous work last trade deadline and will have three first-round picks next year, giving them great flexibility.AFC North
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Baltimore Ravens: CThe Ravens needed to make a move for a quarterback -- Joe Fagnano simply wasn't going to cut it -- and they did, paying a reasonable price, given the situation, for Jacoby Brissett. Best-case scenario, the Ravens stay alive long enough for Lamar Jackson to return. Worst-case scenario, at least they have a workable product. Trading for center Ryan Neuzil right at the deadline buzzer was an interesting move considering Baltimore had already traded for Cam Jurgens earlier this season; perhaps Neuzil moves to guard. The Jurgens move was a bit of an overpay.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Cincinnati Bengals: FThe Bengals would hypothetically get a C for their effort on Tuesday, but they earned an F for the execution. They aimed to add EDGE Arnold Ebiketie from the Eagles on deadline day, but the deal fell through after Cincinnati realized it would have lost its 2027 third-round compensation pick by acquiring Ebiketie. Oops! Bad look by Cincy, which did not end up making any moves.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Cleveland Browns: B-The Browns held firm at the trade deadline, neither buying nor selling. Names such as wide receiver Jerry Jeudy's were in the rumor mill, but it's fine that Cleveland didn't make a move. He has ceded targets to talented rookies Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion, but he is still playing over 60% of the team's offensive snaps. The Browns will battle for a playoff spot or at least to play spoiler and look to really make strides in 2027, when Deshaun Watson's contract ends.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Pittsburgh Steelers: C-The Steelers were reportedly on the hunt for a wide receiver, but nothing materialized for the AFC North leaders. Cornerback reinforcements might have been nice as well, considering the past health issues of Jamel Dean and Asante Samuel Jr. and the age of Jalen Ramsey, but for now, Pittsburgh will look to keep it rolling with the group it has.AFC South
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Houston Texans: C-The Texans paid more for the name than the game when they traded for Marvin Harrison Jr., sending a second-round pick to the Cardinals for a player who hasn't come close to living up to the hype. Harrison is yet to top three catches in any of his three games for Houston this season, and he still played less than half of his new team's snaps coming out of the bye in Week 9. Unless he becomes a more major contributor soon, the overpay looks even worse.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Indianapolis Colts: D+The Colts were the busiest sellers, sending Quenton Nelson to Seattle, Buckner and Keenan Allen to San Francisco and Josh Downs to Kansas City, but them not trading Jonathan Taylor was a gigantic missed opportunity. Taylor is almost 28 years old, and keeping him will only add wear and tear on his body. A contending team likely would have paid more now, with a half-season to go, then next year, when he will only be older and more worn down. The Colts have no chance of contending soon, either. Furthermore, the Colts also decided against moving Grover Stewart, who reportedly garnered mid-round pick interest. One can also wonder if the Colts got enough in the trades they did make, especially for Buckner.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Jacksonville Jaguars: C+The Jaguars did well acquiring safety Jessie Bates III, even if second- and fifth-round picks were a bit pricey. Bates is a tremendous playmaker (28 career interceptions, 14 career forced fumbles) joining a play-making unit; Jacksonville's defense has forced 15 turnovers, third-most this season. After losing defensive tackle DaVon Hamilton for the season, getting defensive tackle Davon Godchaux to help in the middle was reasonable. But a first-round pick and a second-round pick for hulking defensive tackle Jordan Davis was a massive overpay, even if Davis were playing like he did last year, which was a contract year. He's a one-dimensional run plugger who had nine tackles for loss in 2025; he has eight in the rest of his career combined. The Jaguars paid a near-Jeffery Simmons price for a player nowhere near Simmons in terms of all-around talent or disruptiveness, even at his best. He can be a good player who helps -- the Jags will hope they get his best now that he's on a winning team -- and stopping the run is important. But from a value perspective, this was a poor deal. Keeping Brian Thomas Jr. was smart. For an all-in season, they had no need to trade him for future assets, and they can revisit a move this coming offseason.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Tennessee Titans: A-Whether the Titans should have parted ways with Simmons or not is worth arguing, but the return is inarguable. Tennessee having extra first-round picks each of the next two years is outstanding business, and Cam Ward's recent improved play should make the Titans feel all the better. The extra picks will allow Tennessee to surround him with talent at several positions. Getting a second-round pick for Hooker is also good work; Tennessee wanted a strong return, and it got it. The Titans had other players to trade away, such as Tony Pollard, and it's worth wondering if they should have. For now, though, keeping a hot hand helps the young quarterback.
AFC West
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Denver Broncos: A-The Broncos quietly made a helpful deal, acquiring Chargers linebacker Daiyan Henley for a couple of mid-round picks. Henley has plateaued a bit the past couple of seasons after a strong start, but he's an impressive athlete who could benefit from a change of scenery. Vance Joseph has gotten the most out of lots of players, and Henley has the tools to be next in line. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Kansas City Chiefs: B+Josh Downs to the Chiefs is one of the best fits of trade season. Downs is a separation machine who beats man coverage in his sleep, adding an element the Chiefs simply didn't have before. Though he isn't a deep threat, he does have more intermediate juice than was being realized in a dismal Colts passing game. Kansas City could have added an offensive lineman or a deep threat, but for now, Downs is good work.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Las Vegas Raiders: ATake it from my Kirk Cousins trade grades: "If you told a Raiders fan before the season that Mendoza would make his first start in Week 10, they'd probably say that's about right. If you told them he'd start because the Raiders got a top-100 pick for Cousins, they'd be very happy with that outcome." Great work from John Spytek and Co., who were probably close to moving onto Fernando Mendoza anyway.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Los Angeles Chargers: D-The 0-8 Chargers made just one move, and it was a small one, sending Daiyan Henley -- once thought of as a defensive cornerstone -- to a division rival. As if this year couldn't get any more painful. Why Khalil Mack remains on this team is a mystery. Everything about this team remains a mystery.NFC East
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Dallas Cowboys: B-The Cowboys acquired Joey Porter Jr. from the Steelers back at the start of October but smartly stood pat at the trade deadline. For all the offensive firepower, this is a team that is just 4-5 on the season and unable to consistently get stops on defense. Nothing available at the deadline -- outside of a massive overpay -- would have drastically changed that. On the other side, it didn't make much sense to sell, especially if Dallas is hoping to salvage something this year. Rather, the Cowboys will hope their injured players get healthy and can contribute to a second-half charge.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    New York Giants: BThe Giants were a popular hypothetical trade destination as the deadline neared, but they ended up keeping the roster as is. The J.J. McCarthy trade from September has already paid dividends in terms of keeping the Giants' offense moving and the team atop the NFC East for now, but there was no need to force anything if it wasn't developing. An extra defensive lineman might have been nice, but patience is a virtue in this case.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Philadelphia Eagles: APhiladelphia wrestling away a first-round and a second-round pick from the Jaguars for Jordan Davis is marvelous work from Howie Roseman. The move not only adds to the Eagles' deep bag of draft picks, but it potentially frees up the cap space for them to keep Moro Ojomo. The Jurgens trade was also a win, as the Ravens' season has gone off course. This is a wretched season for the Eagles, but the fact that they continue to get massive returns for players whose names are bigger than their games is outstanding. The Eagles now own 10 first- or second-round picks between 2027 and 2029 and will have major roster-building, trade and financial flexibility.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Washington Commanders: D+The Commanders sat and watched another NFC East team amid a lost season make a fortune selling off a pair of players. Washington wouldn't have made a fortune, but it has some players who would have seemingly gathered interest, such as veteran edge defenders K'Lavon Chaisson and Dorance Armstrong and cornerback Rasul Douglas, all set to be free agents after the year. If Washington believes it can make a playoff push, it has badly misjudged the situation.NFC North
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Chicago Bears: AThe Jeffery Simmons trade was Chicago's all-in move, and so far it has been worth it and then some. Simmons has two sacks, three tackles for loss and 10 tackles in two games with Chicago. Was it extremely expensive? Yes. But his impact has matched the price tag, and the Bears very much look like a top-tier Super Bowl contender. 

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Detroit Lions: B-The Lions added Cisco to a secondary that needed help, even with Brian Branch back. Kerby Joseph is yet to return, and Cisco provides some cheap, experienced depth at the very least. He's only 26 years old, and he had seven interceptions from 2022-23 with the Jaguars. Things didn't go as planned in New York, but he could be an important contributor. Another addition, perhaps at corner, would have pushed this grade up.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Green Bay Packers: C+The Packers have found their stride on both sides of the ball, with Jordan Love playing like an MVP frontrunner and the defense surging under Jonathan Gannon. The Packers' real midseason addition will be Micah Parsons, who is due back from injury shortly. An addition in the trenches could have been helpful.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Minnesota Vikings: B-More from my Cousins trade grades: "This all comes down to fit. Kyler Murray never fit. Cousins, hypothetically, does. ... He attacks the middle of the field and delivers on intermediate throws. Plus, he is comfortable off play action. ... Even with a truly outstanding defense, is average-to-slightly-above-average quarterback play and, in turn, average offense good enough to cash in on Super Bowl aspirations? The Vikings are about to find out, but at least they're giving themselves a chance."
NFC South
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Atlanta Falcons: A-Trading away Bates must have been painful for Atlanta. He is a terrific player, one of the smartest in the league and a leader. Even at 3-6, the Falcons are in the thick of things in the woeful NFC South. But this was outstanding value for a soon-to-be 30-year-old who is in the final year of his deal. Plus, the Falcons weren't likely to benefit from compensatory picks if he left this offseason; they have so much money to spend, their additions would have overridden his loss.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Carolina Panthers: C-The Panthers stood pat when additions at cornerback or offensive line could have been helpful. Carolina has not acquired a player via in-season trade since 2021, so perhaps the inaction was always going to be the case, but it feels like in a winnable NFC South, the Panthers could have done something to up their chances.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    New Orleans Saints: B+The Saints moved Godchaux, a veteran defensive tackle whose playing time was dwindling, and got compensation for it. It's a basic move, but there was no reason not to make it, hence a strong mark.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Tampa Bay Buccaneers: C+Tampa Bay could have made a move for a helpful wide receiver here, but it opted not to. The Buccaneers are a pound-the-ball-and-play-defense operation now, but the wide receiver shortcomings were on display throughout their "Sunday Night Football" loss to the Bears, a winnable game. Jason Leicht isn't a huge trade guy, but a low-risk swing could have worked.NFC West
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Arizona Cardinals: B-On one hand, the Cardinals did a commendable job getting so much out of the Harrison trade and for getting even more resources out of the Brissett trade, which occurred after Brissett had been benched. On the other hand, this could have been so much more. Budda Baker went untraded ... again. Josh Sweat didn't go anywhere, either. There's been some really good stuff out of Arizona this year, and the team is far more competitive than expected, but it's a glass half-full, half-empty feeling.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Los Angeles Rams: DThe star-studded, must-win-now Rams are in line to start some combination of Tutu Atwell, CJ Daniels, Konata Mumpfield and/or Xavier Smith at wide receiver for the foreseeable future. Could they have not given up a mid-round pick for someone more reliable for a few weeks? The Rams have climbed to 5-4 after a miserable start, but the job's not close to done.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    San Francisco 49ers: AThe 49ers got great deals on two veterans who can still contribute at positions of need. Buckner is having one of the best years of his career, and San Francisco got him at a perfectly reasonable price. Allen is a reliable slot option who joins an aging wide receiver group riddled by injuries. He can still move the chains on third downs, and if nothing else, he simply provides a capable pass catcher for Brock Purdy. Those are extremely valuable come the stretch run and the postseason; just ask the Rams, don't have them.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Seattle Seahawks: B+Seattle added one of the best guards of this era in Nelson, a crucial add given the interior offensive line struggles. The price wasn't a bargain, but it wasn't overboard, either. The Seahawks were briefly mentioned in the Taylor sweepstakes (won by nobody), but with Jadarian Price and Zach Charbonnet back, they wisely held off.

title: MLB rumors: Mets to meet with Tarik Skubal, Rangers' Corey Seager plan, plus Blue Jays, Cubs, Red Sox, more - CBS Sports
description: Here are your hot stove rumors as the GM meetings open on Tuesday, Nov. 10
body:
Here are your hot stove rumors as the GM meetings open on Tuesday, Nov. 10
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 10, 2026
                            
                    at
    5:21 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            7 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        This is an important week on the baseball calendar. First and foremost, it is awards week. Kevin McGonigle and Sal Stewart were named the Rookies of the Year on Monday. The Managers of the Year will be announced Tuesday, Cy Youngs and Relievers of the Year will be announced Wednesday, and finally the MVPs will be announced Thursday.   Also, the GM Meetings are this week in Las Vegas. The GM Meetings are not the Winter Meetings in terms of the sheer volume of rumors and transactions, but they do usually provide some news. There could be more than usual this year given the near certainty of a lockout on Dec. 1, which would also mean there are no Winter Meetings. This may be the only time everyone is in the same room this winter. The three weeks between now and Dec. 1 could be quite active.   We've already ranked the top 50 free agents and the top 25 trade candidates.   With that in mind, here are Tuesday's hot stove rumors.  
                            
    
                                                
                    
     Mets will meet with Skubal 
The Mets have a meeting scheduled with two-time Cy Young winner Tarik Skubal, the clear top free agent avaiable this offseason, later this week, reports the New York Post. Skubal will meet with teams in California, presumably at the offices of agent Scott Boras. Owner Steve Cohen is expected to push for Skubal, according to SNY; president of baseball operations David Stearns has long been reluctant to sign big-money, long-term deals for pitchers, though pitchers of Skubal's caliber are rarely available. The Mets are also seeking first base help and bullpen reinforcements.Nolan McLean and Christian Scott are the only locks for New York's 2027 rotation at the moment. Justin Hagenman, Sean Manaea, Kodai Senga, Zac Thornton, and Jonah Tong are next in line to make starts. Tylor Megill is expected back from Tommy John surgery early next year as well. The Mets have some depth but clearly need more impact. 

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Rangers to "explore" trading Corey SeagerThe Rangers signed Corey Seager to a 10-year, $325 million deal prior to the 2022 season and it paid off quite handsomely with a World Series title in 2023 (Seager was the World Series MVP). With five years and roughly $155 million left on the deal, however, the Rangers appear ready to trade him. The Rangers "intend to explore moving Seager at the general managers' meetings," reports The Athletic.Seager, 32, was stellar from 2023 to 2025 in spite of a litany of injuries, averaging 6.2 WAR per season with a .294 average and 158 OPS+. He actually averaged 8.7 WAR per 162 games. Only the injuries kept him from making multiple serious MVP runs. Last season, though, was a step back. In 102 games, he hit .227/.312/.424 with 20 home runs, 51 RBI and 3.1 WAR. 
The injury history keeps getting more extensive, too, as he's dealt with injuries to his thumb, hamstring, hip, other hamstring and back in the last four years. With a lackluster, at best, shortstop class in free agency, now might be the perfect time for the Rangers to move on from Seager, assuming a deal can be worked out with the years and dollars left on his contract. Texas also has Sebastian Walcott, one of the top prospects in baseball, ready in the wings.
                            
    
                                                
                    
     Blue Jays interested in Lowe 
The Blue Jays are among the teams with interest in free agent second baseman Brandon Lowe, according to Sportsnet. Ernie Clement, Toronto's primary second baseman in 2026, crashed hard in the second half and has always fit better as a super utility man who plays regularly at different positions. Josh Smith is the team's other second base option. 
Lowe would bring needed power to a team that finished dead last in home runs this past season and had just one player, Kazuma Okamoto (33), clear 15 home runs. Only four Blue Jays hit even 10 homers. Also, Toronto's lineup is mostly right-handed. Lowe would add power and also a lefty bat to provide balance. We ranked him as the 13th-best free agent available. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
     Rotation help a 'top priority' for White Sox Adding rotation help is a "top priority," White Sox GM Chris Getz said during an MLB Network Radio interview on Tuesday. "We're going to exhaust the starter market, both free agency -- we'll take a look -- along with trades. That is our top priority," Getz said. He also confirmed that Grant Taylor, the team's postseason closer, will move into the rotation. Hagen Smith will remain in the bullpen. The White Sox have solid enough rotation depth with Taylor joining Sean Burke, Luis Castillo, Anthony Kay, Davis Martin, David Sandlin, Noah Schultz, and perhaps Shane Smith and Drew Thorpe. There is room for improvement, though, particularly at the top. Chicago could use a bona fide ace, not that one is easy to acquire or abundantly available. 

                            
    
                                                
                    
       Padres have expressed interest in Skubal   Add the Padres to the list of teams that have shown interest in Skubal, reports MLB Network. San Diego has a major need in the rotation -- Joe Musgrove, who hasn't made a start since the 2024 postseason, and Randy Vásquez are their only rotation locks -- and a new ownership group that seems willing to spend in its first offseason.   Skubal is far and away the offseason's best free agent. He is also a Scott Boras client, and, historically, top Boras clients take the largest contract offer regardless of team situation. That isn't to say the Padres are a bad situation. Not at all. They're a very good team that is in the postseason most years, plus they play in San Diego. Who doesn't love San Diego?   The Padres are also connected to several Japanese players, according to The Athletic. That includes MLB free agents Seiya Suzuki and Shota Imanaga, as well as players coming over from Nippon Professional Baseball, like third baseman Teruaki Sato. 

        
            
                MLB free agency: Six international players to know for the 2026-27 offseason
                
                    Mike Axisa                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
   Morejon prefers to stay in the bullpen   
Free agent lefty Adrian Morejon is drawing interest as a starting pitcher, but he prefers to remain in the bullpen, according to The Athletic. Even during the season, there were rumblings that Morejon would like to be given a chance to start in 2027. He came up through the minors as a starter and only remained in the bullpen because he was so dominant in a late-inning role.   We ranked Morejon as the offseason's second-best free agent on the idea that he would move into the rotation. The belief within the game is that he has a chance to be an excellent starter, not just a back-end piece. Either way, Morejon is a very good pitcher, and at 28, he's also one of the youngest free agents available. He should have several peak years remaining.   
                            
    
                                                
                    
     Cubs hope to add three starters Although they are disinclined to pursue Tarik Skubal, the Cubs hope to add three established starting pitchers this offseason, reports The Athletic. Of the nine pitchers to make at least nine starts for Chicago in 2027, seven are free agents. Only Ben Brown, who recently had neck surgery (per ESPN), and Edward Cabrera, who had a 5.96 ERA and was demoted to the bullpen, remain. 
Left-hander Justin Steele is expected back from UCL surgery next year, though he suffered a setback this summer and wasn't able to return as hoped in September. Others like Javier Assad and Jordan Wicks are depth options more than full-time rotation pieces. This free agent class offers plenty of second- and third-tier starters. That's where the Cubs are expected to shop. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
       Mets not interested in major overhaul   Unlike last offseason, the Mets are not interested in a major overhaul despite their disappointing year, reports MLB.com. The Mets went 74-88 and finished in last place in 2026. The only silver lining to the disappointing season was the ability to give a long runway to rookies like Carson Benge and Nolan McLean, both of whom finished in the top four of the Rookie of the Year voting.   The Mets went 83-79 in 2025 and missed the postseason on the final day of the season. They made significant changes last winter, most notably jettisoning stalwarts Pete Alonso and Brandon Nimmo, then had a worse season in 2026. In September, president of baseball operations David Stearns admitted that much turnover created an "uncapped downside scenario," which is executive-speak for "there was too much risk." 

                            
    
                                                
                    
       Braves will not move Acuña   
Not surprisingly, the Braves are uninterested in moving former National League MVP Ronald Acuña Jr., according to MLB Network. It does feel like Atlanta's offense has gone stale and that they could move a core piece, but it won't be Acuña, nor is it likely to be Drake Baldwin, Michael Harris II, or Matt Olson. Ozzie Albies and Austin Riley are the more obvious players to move. Albies is entering the final season of his wildly team-friendly contract. Riley has six years remaining on his deal, which figures to make a move difficult.   
                            
    
                                                
                    
       Red Sox won't commit to Story at short   
On Monday, Red Sox chief baseball officer Craig Breslow declined to commit to Trevor Story as his starting shortstop next season. "We still have a ton of confidence in Trevor, but any decisions like that are going to take place between Trevor and me far before I speak to anything publicly," Breslow told reporters, including the Boston Globe. Boston has one of the top prospects in the minors in shortstop Franklin Arias, who is very likely to make his debut early next year. Arias could push Story into a utility role or off the team entirely.

body:
Blue Jays general manager Ross Atkins said he told Santander that he needed to address his comments publicly

        Blue Jays general manager Ross Atkins had strong words Tuesday in reaction to Anthony Santander's anti-Muslim social media posts that he has since deleted."There really aren't words to express my level of disappointment," Atkins said from the GM meetings on Tuesday, via Sportsnet. "Anything exacerbating some level of hate, anti-Islamic, is just extremely concerning and extremely disappointing."I also talked to Anthony about his lack of awareness, realizing that he has a very large microphone, what that meant. We're working exceptionally hard internally to ensure, and we have been, that it's a safe environment, that baseball is for everyone. It's very important to us. It's a part of our organizational values and his behavior did not align with that."  Santander, a native Venezuelan, shared social media videos in the wake of the U.S. midterm elections last week, including one where a Christian pastor said, "there is no such thing as kind Muslims." Another implied that Sharia law would be imposed in the U.S. following the election of Abdul El-Sayed to the Senate. Santander has since taken down the videos from his social media pages. In the aftermath, the team released the following statement: 
"Baseball is for everyone, and the Blue Jays have created an inclusive experience where all fans feel welcome at our ballpark. Individual comments do not represent our organization's values and beliefs."It's unclear whether Santander plans to address the matter publicly, but Atkins said he "told him that I thought he needed to and that he should." As far as personal conversations with Santander, Atkins said, "I expressed my level of concern. I believe he felt it. I know he feels badly. But I don't want to speak for him."  
Santander was signed as an amateur free agent out of Venezuela in 2011 when he was 16. He signed a free agent deal with the Blue Jays prior to the 2025 season; injuries have held him to just 54 games in the past two seasons.

body:
Alabama and UCLA join Georgia and Utah with first-round byes, while Indiana's tumble costs the reigning champions home-field advantage and Notre Dame surges into prime host position
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 10, 2026

        Georgia surged to No. 1 in the College Football Playoff Rankings, but it was the lower spots that completely reshaped the bracket. Alabama surged to No. 3 after its win over LSU, while UCLA moved to No. 4. The Bulldogs, No. 2 Utah, Tide and Bruins are the four projected byes in the bracket. Despite not playing, reigning national champion Indiana dropped five spots to the No. 9 seed, going all the way from a first-round bye to not even hosting a playoff game. Conversely, Notre Dame went from the last team into the field to the top first-round host after outlasting Miami in Week 10. After the rankings, No. 5 Notre Dame, No. 6 Texas, No. 7 Miami and No. 8 Tennessee are projected as the four first round hosts. No. 11 Kentucky is the last team in the field, while No. 12 Texas Tech and No. 13 Wake Forest sit right outside the bubble. Here is how the College Football Playoff bracket looks after the second CFP Rankings release of the 2026 season. 
Notre Dame surgesLast week, Notre Dame was projected as the 11-seed and final at-large team in the College Football Playoff rankings. After beating then-No. 1 Miami, the Fighting Irish jumped several spots to No. 5, where they projected as a first-round host against 12-seed Boise State. That would feature a next step against a feisty-but-beatable No. 4 UCLA squad in the second round before getting their shot against No. 1 Georgia. Getting back to the national semifinals would be a huge step -- and they would become the new favorite if they knocked off the Dawgs. Indiana's a big loserDespite not playing because of a bye week, Indiana dramatically fell in the bracket, from a first-round bye to not even hosting a home game. The Hoosiers have not played well over the past several weeks, and every one of their quality wins picked up yet another loss to ding them in the rankings. 
Now, instead of earning a second straight first round bye, Indiana will instead have to sweat it out just to host a first round game. That would set up a tough road game at Neyland Stadium against 8-seed Tennessee before playing 1-seed Georgia in the second round. That's untenable for nearly any team. Big 12 positioned wellThe conference was one of the biggest losers of the first playoff rankings, but they're riding much higher in the second. Despite a loss to Utah, No. 10 BYU is finally getting the credit for beating a highly ranked Notre Dame, meaning they remain in the rankings with room to spare. Even if the league falters, there are a few contingency plans. No. 12 Texas Tech is the first team out, leaving them in good shape. No. 14 Houston is also within striking distance. While No. 23 Arizona and No. 25 Oklahoma State probably can't rise all the way to the field, they can help raise resumes. 
The Big 12 has not produced an at-large CFP team in the 12-team era, the only Power Four league that has failed to do so.

body:
Jocytė, the No. 5 pick in the 2025 draft, didn't see much time this season, but could be an important part of the Valkyries' future
